# truefoundry_role_binding (Resource)

Manages a TrueFoundry role binding (`role-binding` manifest): grants roles on resources to users, teams, virtual accounts, or agents. Role bindings replace the per-resource `collaborators` and the virtual account `permissions`, which TrueFoundry retires on 15 Nov 2026.

A binding has either **one subject with many permissions** or **many subjects with one permission**, never many of both — split it into one binding per role to give several subjects several roles. The control plane matches bindings by name, so applying a name that already exists takes that binding over.

Import an existing binding by its name: `terraform import truefoundry_role_binding.example my-binding`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# One subject with many permissions: a virtual account that may use two
# provider accounts and an MCP server.
resource "truefoundry_role_binding" "ci_bot" {
  name = "va-ci-bot"

  subjects = [
    { type = "virtualaccount", name = "ci-bot" },
  ]

  permissions = [
    {
      resource_type = "provider-account"
      resource_fqn  = "my-tenant:azure-openai:my-azure-openai"
      role          = "provider-account-access"
    },
    {
      resource_type = "provider-account"
      resource_fqn  = truefoundry_custom_endpoint_account.speech.fqn
      role          = "provider-account-access"
    },
    {
      resource_type = "mcp-server"
      resource_fqn  = truefoundry_mcp_server.deepwiki.fqn
      role          = "mcp-server-user"
    },
  ]
}

# Many subjects with one permission: who manages a guardrail group. To give
# several subjects several roles, use one binding per role.
resource "truefoundry_role_binding" "guardrail_managers" {
  name = "guardrails-francecentral-managers"

  subjects = [
    { type = "user", name = "jane@example.com" },
    { type = "team", name = "ai-platform" },
  ]

  permissions = [
    {
      resource_type = "provider-account"
      resource_fqn  = truefoundry_guardrail_group.region.fqn
      role          = "provider-account-manager"
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the role binding (3-66 characters; must start with a lowercase letter, end with a letter or digit, and contain only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens), unique within the tenant. Changing it replaces the binding.
- `permissions` (Attributes Set) Roles granted on resources. More than one permission requires exactly one subject. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--permissions))
- `subjects` (Attributes Set) Principals the permissions are granted to. More than one subject requires exactly one permission. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--subjects))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Control plane ID of the role binding.

<a id="nestedatt--permissions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `permissions`

Required:

- `resource_fqn` (String) FQN of the resource, e.g. the `fqn` attribute of a `truefoundry_custom_endpoint_account` or `truefoundry_guardrail_group`.
- `resource_type` (String) Kind of resource the role applies to, e.g. `provider-account`, `mcp-server`, `secret-group`, `ml-repo`, `workspace`.
- `role` (String) Role to grant on the resource, e.g. `provider-account-access` or `mcp-server-user`.


<a id="nestedatt--subjects"></a>
### Nested Schema for `subjects`

Required:

- `name` (String) Email address for `user`; the team, virtual account, or agent name otherwise.
- `type` (String) Kind of principal. One of: `user`, `team`, `virtualaccount`, `agent`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Role bindings are imported by their name.
terraform import truefoundry_role_binding.ci_bot va-ci-bot
```
